messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from the CP/VPC egress RFC — we need a short decision on ephemeral NAT64 failover semantics for IPv6-only customers. Do we preserve src IP across peered controlplane vs relay egress, or accept SNAT when falling back to regional relay?

priya: TL;DR: preserving src IP is ideal for customer ACLs, but it's heavier on ops (IP inventory + rotation).

sam: Also: if we require srcip preservation across peering, we either: 1) keep per-tenant ENIs / static IPs, or 2) punch holes in customer's routing. Both add cost.

jordan: Implementation notes: conntrack + NAT64 translation state is tied to 5-tuple. If we SNAT during failover, existing connections will break. Need session-sticky fallback or orchestrated drain.

elena: Suggestion: permit SNAT on fallback but provide a short-lived tcp-proxy (L4) to preserve existing connections during cutover. New flows after failover get SNAT.

alex: Could we use a short grace window (e.g., 60s) where the connector rewrites packets to preserve 5-tuple semantics? If we do that we must sync translation mapping from peering -> relay. Complexity: high.

priya: Another option: advertise per-tenant ephemeral IP pool from our side and failover simply reassigns the same ephemeral IP to the relay. Requires L2/ENI-level control on relay nodes.

sam: That's effectively doing our own IP mobility. Ops concerns: IP exhaustion, rotation TTL, and cross-account security approvals.

jordan: If we accept SNAT, customers with ACLs that match source IP will break. Could we expose a compatibility hook in control plane: a boolean egress:preserve_src that triggers dedicated IP reservation?

elena: That feels OK — preserve_src=true -> reserved IP + billing note. preserve_src=false -> cheap failover (SNAT on relay).

ops-bot: NOTE: current relays support SNAT and can accept additional ENIs on demand, but ENI attach latency ~20s in us-west-2 during peak.

priya: We'll need clear docs: "compat_mode: preserve-src requires reserved egress IPs and longer onboarding; default is compat_mode: best-effort (SNAT on fallback)."

alex: Decision proposal: 1) Default behavior = allow SNAT on fallback (lowest ops/cost). 2) Offer opt-in preserve_src flag that provisions ephemeral reserved IPs and an observability hook showing failover events. 3) Implement a short connection drain proxy (L4) as mitigation for mid-flight breaks.

sam: +1 for opt-in. Need to quantify cost delta (reserved IPs, ENI ops) before we ship.

jordan: I'll sketch the implementation: control plane will issue a reserved-IP lease (duration TTL), relay subscribes and attaches ENI; during failover we hand the same lease to relay and update BGP/NAT mapping. Proxy is sticky per-connection and runs as sidecar on relay nodes.

elena: Can we reuse existing egress-operator APIs? If yes we should avoid new surface area.

alex: Action items: jordan -> design doc for preserve_src flow + conntrack migration plan; elena -> egress-operator compatibility check; priya -> short customer-facing doc + pricing blurb; sam -> cost estimate. We'll aim for a decision checkpoint next week.

priya: minor: include IPv6-only testing matrix e.g., DNS64, NAT64 translation edgecases.

jordan: noted. I'll add a test plan with synthetic flows and long-lived tcp connections.

alex: Thanks all. If nobody objects, I'll mark RFC follow-up as "opt-in preserve-src with default SNAT fallback" in the architecture tracker later today. :thumbsup:

elena: no objections from me.

sam: no objections.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Reminder: any ENI-provisioning automation changes need a runbook update (oncall will require a rollback path).
